name: plotly

files.tests/test_figures.py:
from app import figures


def test_sales_scatter(df):
    fig = figures.sales_scatter(df)
    assert fig.layout.title.text == "Visits vs sales"
    assert fig.layout.title.font.size == 18
    assert len(fig.data) == 4


def test_styled_axes(df):
    fig = figures.styled_axes(figures.sales_scatter(df), "visits", "sales")
    assert fig.layout.xaxis.title.text == "visits"
    assert fig.layout.yaxis.title.font.size == 12


def test_busy_hours():
    fig = figures.busy_hours([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
    assert [list(row) for row in fig.data[0].z] == [[1, 2], [3, 4]]


def test_shop_map(df):
    fig = figures.shop_map(df)
    assert list(fig.data[0].lat) == [52.37, 51.92, 52.09, 51.44]


def test_side_by_side(df):
    fig = figures.side_by_side(df)
    assert [t.type for t in fig.data] == ["bar", "scatter"]
    assert fig.data[1].xaxis == "x2"

notes: Old: plotly 5.24.1 on Python 3.11 (the last 5.x). New: 6.9.0 on Python 3.12, the newest 6.x (7.x exists; 5 -> 6 is the migration people face). pandas 2.2.3 and numpy 1.26.4 are the same on both sides so only plotly moves (narwhals comes in with plotly 6). titlefont goes through update_layout(**kwargs) / update_xaxes(**kwargs), so the call binds and the generated validators raise ValueError: no signature change on the called method (go.Layout.__init__ does lose titlefont). make_subplots and append_trace warn on both sides: they are DEPRECATED, not breaks. The default 'plotly' template differs only in the heatmapgl/scattermap entries, so figure objects are not equal in full between the versions even after migration; the equivalent tests only read data and layout fields. Not covered: colorbar titleside (a dict key), go.Pointcloud, write_image (needs kaleido), to_json of a whole figure (the embedded template changes).
